meta.description: Canonical example for AI agents generating importable my-slides JSON.
meta.author: my-slides
meta.purpose: Copy structure and field names; replace title, slug, and slide markdown with the user's topic.

slides.markdown:
# Presentation title

Subtitle or event name · Speaker name
slides.notes: Open with the topic and who is presenting. Keep title slide to one headline plus one supporting line.

slides.markdown:
## Section: context

One line on what this section covers
slides.notes: Use section slides to divide major parts of the talk.

slides.markdown:
## Key points

- First idea stated in plain language
- Second idea with a concrete detail
- Third idea and why it matters

**Takeaway:** one sentence the audience should remember.
slides.notes: Prefer 3–5 bullets per slide. Put the takeaway in bold on the last line when useful.

slides.markdown:
## Example: code or config

```bash
npm run dev
```

```json
{ "version": 1, "title": "My deck" }
```
slides.notes: Use fenced code blocks for commands, JSON, or snippets. One concept per slide.

slides.markdown:
## Compare or contrast

**Option A**

- Pro one
- Pro two

---

**Option B**

- Pro one
- Pro two
slides.notes: For two-column layout, separate columns with a horizontal rule `---` on its own line in markdown when it reads better as two blocks.

slides.markdown:
## Quick reference

| Field | Required | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | yes | `1` |
| `title` | yes | `"Q4 review"` |
| `slides` | yes | array of slide objects |
| `templateId` | no | `"astro"`, `"dark"`, `"default"` |
| `visibility` | no | `"public"` or `"authenticated"` |
slides.notes: Tables work in markdown. Escape backticks inside table cells if needed.

slides.markdown:
## Slide with custom background

This slide sets `background` to a dark color (see JSON).
slides.notes: Optional per-slide background: hex color, or Reveal.js image URL syntax if you use a full URL in the background field.
End slide: thanks, link, or call to action.
